name: PingOne
scope_notes: Covers PingOne (PingOne Platform / Management APIs). SaaS; covers PingOne platform Worker apps and gateway credentials; inbound traffic policies need a Cloudflare-based custom domain.

controls.name: Application enable/disable toggle
controls.what: Disables a Worker app so it cannot be used.
controls.setting: Applications > Applications > (app) > toggle; API: PUT application enabled=false

controls.name: Role assignments (Roles tab / roleAssignments API)
controls.what: Worker app access equals its admin role assignments, scoped to org, environment, population, group, or application, and checked on each API call.

controls.name: assignActorRoles
controls.what: When false, an API-created Worker app does not inherit the creator's roles.

controls.name: Generate New Secret
controls.what: Replaces the client secret and keeps the previous one valid for a chosen window (1 minute to 90 days).
controls.setting: Applications > (app) > Configuration > Generate New Secret; application secret API

controls.name: Revoke Previous Client Secret
controls.what: Ends the grace period for the old secret immediately.
controls.setting: Applications > (app) > Configuration > Revoke Previous Client Secret

controls.name: Refresh Token Duration
controls.what: Sets refresh token lifetime (default 30 days, 60 seconds to 1826 days).

controls.name: Inbound traffic policies
controls.what: Allow or block requests by CIDR and other verify rules, only on Cloudflare-based custom domains.

controls.name: Delete Gateway Credentials
controls.what: Deletes and revokes a gateway credential for all instances using it.

controls.name: Delete application
controls.what: Removes the Worker app and its secret (logged as APPLICATION.DELETED).

controls.name: Environment Admin role required for gateway entities
controls.what: Only admins with the Environment Admin role can create or manage gateway credentials.

no_control.what: Issued PingOne API (Management API) access tokens cannot be revoked; they stay valid until expiry (60 min default).
Access tokens for the PingOne API resource cannot be revoked via /as/revoke.

controls_unknown: Whether disabling the app or rotating the secret invalidates already-issued access tokens (role removal does take effect per call per S5)
Whether successful client_credentials token issuance produces an audit event
Whether Management API read calls (e.g., GET users) are audited
Whether inbound traffic policies apply to api.pingone.com
Admin-level policy to block Worker app creation or require approval
Gateway credential expiry and whether its creation/deletion has a distinct audit event
Maximum configurable access token lifetime for the PingOne API resource

authentication.summary: A Worker app authenticates to POST /{envID}/as/token with its client ID and secret (or client_secret_jwt / private_key_jwt) and gets a 60-minute JWT access token. The token has admin-level access to the PingOne Management APIs, limited by the app's own role assignments. No user signs in, so sign-on policies and MFA do not apply to it (docs describe it as a userless app; no explicit SSO-bypass statement).

federation.details: Docs describe client secret and private_key_jwt client authentication; no workload identity federation for Worker apps was found.

ip_restriction.boundary: Inbound traffic policies (IP allow/block via CIDR verify rules) exist only for Cloudflare-based custom domains. Docs do not say they cover api.pingone.com Management API calls or the default auth.pingone.com token endpoint.

lifetime.summary: Access token 60 min; client secret has no documented expiry

renewal.expiry_basis: Secret is long-lived until rotated; app requests a new token with the same secret
renewal.summary: No refresh token; reuse the client secret. On rotation the previous secret can stay valid 1 minute to 90 days.

administration.summary: Admins create Worker apps and assign admin roles scoped to org, environment, population, group, or application. Apps created via API inherit the creator's roles unless assignActorRoles=false. Apps can be disabled with the toggle; removing all roles blocks token issuance.
administration.conditions: An actor cannot grant roles it lacks; reading the secret requires a superset of the app's roles.

offboard.details: client_credentials tokens use the application's own role assignments, not a user's.

inventory.details: GET /v1/environments/{envID}/applications lists all applications, including Worker apps, per environment.

token_format.notes: Access token is an RS256 JWT; client secret is at least 64 characters for PingOne-generated secrets.

log_sources.notes: Configuration events kept 2 years, user events 90 days; queries max 14 days; Audit API rate 10/second.

log_sources.name: Subscriptions (webhooks)
log_sources.notes: Streams audit events to HTTPS/TCP endpoints; events lost if target down >7 days.

Application ID on APPLICATION.* / SECRET.* events

containment.steps: Generate a new secret and revoke the previous secret, remove role assignments, or disable/delete the app. Existing access tokens cannot be revoked; removing roles cuts access on the next call.
containment.notes: Role removal is checked per call (S5); token revocation is not available for PingOne API tokens (S8).

unknown: No documented whoami endpoint for client_credentials tokens

authentication.summary: An interactive Worker app signs in an admin user through PingOne and gets an access token that carries that user's admin role assignments. The token calls the Management APIs as the user.

federation.details: User-delegated token; user sign-in may itself be federated to an external IdP.

ip_restriction.boundary: Same as pingone-1: inbound traffic policies only on Cloudflare custom domains; coverage of Management API calls not documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token 60 min; refresh token 30 days default, up to 1826 days

renewal.expiry_basis: refreshTokenDuration on the app (rolling duration also configurable)
renewal.summary: If refresh tokens are enabled, new access tokens are minted without the user signing in again.

administration.summary: Access is bounded by the user's own role assignments, re-checked on each API call. Admins can disable the app, remove the user's roles, or shorten refresh token duration.
administration.conditions: Refresh tokens for custom resources can be revoked at /as/revoke; PingOne API resource tokens cannot.

sso.details: The token is issued after the user signs in through the authentication policies assigned on the Worker app's Policies tab.

inventory.details: GET /v1/environments/{envID}/applications lists the Worker apps, but not the user tokens issued through them.

sso.ui: Applications > Applications > [Worker app] > Policies > Pencil > select PingOne/DaVinci policies > Save

token_format.notes: RS256 JWT access token; refresh token may be opaque.

log_sources.notes: Configuration events kept 2 years, user events 90 days; queries max 14 days; Audit API rate 10/second.

log_sources.notes: Streams audit events to HTTPS/TCP endpoints; events lost if target down >7 days.

containment.steps: Remove the user's admin roles, disable the app, or delete the user. Revoke refresh tokens at /as/revoke only applies to custom-resource tokens.
containment.notes: PingOne API access tokens cannot be revoked; roles are checked per call.

authentication.summary: A gateway instance (LDAP, PingFederate, RADIUS, API gateway integration, Authorize) running in the customer's infrastructure holds a signed JWT gateway credential. It exchanges the credential at /as/token (token_exchange grant) for an access token to PingOne resources.

federation.details: Static signed JWT issued by PingOne.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP restriction documented for gateway credentials.

lifetime.summary: No expiry documented; claims list has no exp claim

renewal.expiry_basis: Create a new credential (max five per gateway) and delete the old one
renewal.summary: Rotation is manual by issuing a new credential.

administration.summary: Environment Admins create, list, and delete gateway credentials. Deleting a credential revokes it for all gateway instances using it.
administration.conditions: Max five credentials per gateway; token value shown only at creation.

offboard.details: The credential belongs to a gateway instance, not a user.

inventory.details: GET /v1/environments/{envID}/gateways/{gatewayID}/credentials lists credentials per gateway (max five per gateway).

token_format.notes: Signed JWT; iss wss://gateways.pingone.com; jti equals the credential ID.
